terms.meaning: A fixed list of allowed names. A value outside the list is rejected.
A list of allowed words that cannot grow without a deliberate change.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module header and imports
sections.what: Section code was not included in the packet, so its contents are not known. It is the file's opening part, which normally holds the module description and imports.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: StepType
sections.title: Step type categories
sections.what: Section code was not included in the packet, so the exact categories are not known. By name, it defines the closed list of step kinds used in the workflow.
sections.why: Likely reason: a closed list keeps every step labelled in the same few ways so records can be compared.
sections.watch_out: Any new value added here changes what stored records can contain, so check every reader.

sections.name: DebtType
sections.title: Workflow debt catalogue
sections.what: Defines the fixed list of twelve kinds of workflow debt, such as manual re-keying, shadow spreadsheets, email approvals and batch waits. The auditor must pick from this list when it scores a finding, so the same kind of problem gets the same label across processes, clients and years.
sections.why: The docstring states that a closed list is what makes debt comparable. Reason not stated in the code beyond that.
sections.watch_out: Adding or renaming a member changes the labels stored in old records, so treat the list as a contract.

sections.name: Posture
sections.title: Future-state posture levels
sections.what: Defines four levels of how far a redesigned process departs from today: minimal, moderate, substantial and transformational. The feasibility assessor can lower a posture but cannot raise it.
sections.why: The docstring orders these from least to most disruptive, and the one-way rule stops any stage from making a design look bolder than the evidence supports.
sections.watch_out: The order of these levels matters to any code that compares them, so do not reorder them casually.

sections.name: PerformerKind
sections.title: Performer types
sections.what: Defines the two kinds of performer for a future-state step: a designed agent (software) or a named human role.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The split lets the schema check that software steps point to agents that were actually designed.
sections.watch_out: A step labelled as an agent must match an agent name defined elsewhere, or validation fails.

sections.name: HeadcountDirection
sections.title: Headcount direction labels
sections.what: Defines four labels for how a workforce impact moves: increase, decrease, unchanged or reshaped. It deliberately holds no numbers, so the design step cannot produce a staff total.
sections.why: The docstring says FTE totals are computed in the value package from stated parameters, not written by an agent.
sections.watch_out: Do not add a numeric headcount field here. That would let an agent produce a total the design is meant to prevent.

sections.name: PrerequisiteKind
sections.title: Prerequisite categories
sections.what: Defines five kinds of thing that must be in place before a process can go live: another process, a data product, a platform, a control or a capability.
sections.why: The docstring explains that most real prerequisites are not other processes, so a plan limited to process-to-process links would schedule impossible work.
sections.watch_out: Keep this list aligned with the reasons used in the reconciliation module, or prerequisites may fail to map.

sections.name: BlockName
sections.title: Block names for claims
sections.what: Lists the six named parts of a process record that each carry their own confidence score: framing, current state, scorecard, future state, implications and value parameters.
sections.why: The docstring says each block is scored separately so a well-sourced current state cannot hide an invented future state.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a block changes stored records and any code that looks up confidence by block name.

sections.name: EnablerId
sections.title: Shared enabler identifiers
sections.what: Defines the closed list of shared capabilities, each with a code such as PAT-DOC-INTEL for document intelligence. Processes that need the same capability must use the same code so their benefits are counted once.
sections.why: The docstring explains that free-text names let the same capability appear under several spellings, which inflates totals silently.
sections.watch_out: The docstring says not to widen this to free text. An agent that needs a capability not listed will fail validation, so new codes must be added here deliberately.

summary: Holds the closed lists of allowed words used across the schema, so the same term means the same thing on every record. The packet included only the file setup and the step type list, so this note covers only those.
purpose: Keeps categories consistent across records so rollups can group them reliably.
why: The docstring says free-text categories let a taxonomy drift, and the defect stays hidden because each record looks correct on its own.
how: Imports the standard string-enum type and defines each enum as a fixed set of named values. The docstring says a new value must go through a schema change, never by widening a field to accept any text.
inputs: Values written into records by agents or people.
outputs: Restricted values for the fields that use these enums. A value outside the list fails validation.
risks: Widening a field to free text to make a failing agent pass. Adding a value without updating code that depends on the list.
debug: If validation fails with an enum error, the value is outside the allowed list. Compare the value against the list here. If the observation is real, a schema change is needed rather than a looser field.
